origin.description: Draws an object of class Lc, the empirical Lorenz curve.
origin.usage:
plot.Lc(x, general=FALSE, lwd=2, xlab="p", ylab="L(p)",
    main="Lorenz curve", las=1, ...)

arguments.name: general
arguments.text: If TRUE, draw the generalized Lorenz curve instead of the ordinary one.

arguments.name: lwd, xlab, ylab, main, las, ...
arguments.text: Further arguments passed to the high-level plot. Tick labels are horizontal.

origin.details: The ordinates are L when general is FALSE and L.general otherwise. A straight line through the origin with slope equal to the largest ordinate is added, the diagonal of equality for an ordinary curve. lines.Lc is the same curve without that line, drawn onto an existing plot.

translation.description: Draws the empirical Lorenz curve stored in the dict returned by Lc.
translation.usage: plot_lc(x, general=False, lwd=2, xlabel="p", ylabel="L(p)", main="Lorenz curve", ax=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict with NumPy arrays p, L, and L.general, as returned by Lc.

arguments.name: general
arguments.text: If true, draw L.general instead of L.

arguments.name: lwd
arguments.text: Width of the Lorenz curve. The diagonal is a unit-width line.

arguments.name: xlabel, ylabel, main
arguments.text: Axis labels and title. These are xlab, ylab, and main in R.

arguments.name: ax
arguments.text: Axes to draw on. None opens a new figure.

translation.details: The curve is a Matplotlib line of p against L, or against L.general when general is true. A second line runs from (0, 0) to (1, max(y)), matching abline(0, max(L)). Axis limits hug the curve, with no padding.
translation.value: A dict with the plotted coordinates, p and y.
